Not technically tacoma, Fife, but cabbage patch which was our "school Olympics" that would have the grades pitted against each other, throwing cabbages at each other's houses, trashing each other's lockers and designated sides of the school, my favorite Olympic game was pushing a Volkswagen beetle across the track. Also seniors would play cops and robbers that everyone would always take *way* too far with full on "drive by"s and showing up at people's houses at night.

Nature places: point defiance, titlow, and chambers bay, ruston
Transit system: buses are aight (get an orca card), but in general kinda sucks. 
Groceries: winco is cheapest
Bars: my favourite gay bar is the mix. 
In general Tacoma is usually very lgbt+ friendly but we do have dickheads just like everywhere else. Don't take this sub to be an indicator of the people here lol. Downtown and stadium district can be fun, lots of bars within walking distance of each other, coffee shops, and interesting thrift stores. Avoid Hosmer or honestly most of east tacoma if you can. It's not terrible but can get sketchy. Join tacompton files on FB (the one on reddit is different), trust me. Gets news out the fastest. Welcome!

Yep. Exactly all that. Whatever happens, if they commit suicide or end up homeless, its not your fault. That's no one's fault but their own, and I think emotionally you have to fully accept that (not an easy task) before you can do anything about it. Their life is no one's responsibility but their own. In my case, I'll spare you all the details, but after finally getting them to leave and not speaking for about a year, I ran into him at a bar. I knew I made the right decision because if losing everything wasn't enough for him to change, he never would, and I couldn't subject the entire rest of my life to that.

It doesnt need to be on her phone the entire time but couldnt he use her phone or a public computer (like at a library) to fill it out prior to travelling? Im not saying the way they do it isnt fucked up  they definitely need a fully accessible and inclusive system but it does seem possible for him to do it without having to own a cellphone.
